focus.jtag: The Fed's rate call lands this afternoon and two mega-caps report tonight, while a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery re-ignited the oil premium. The scanner boarded WM, CSGP, NXPI, APH, CAKE (Type A) and BUG (Type C)
focus.jnote: The tape is calm but the calendar is loaded. The S&P 500 closed Tuesday at 7,722.60, up 0.6%, while the Nasdaq Composite jumped 1.18% to 26,477.81. Futures traded mixed early Wednesday ahead of Microsoft and Alphabet earnings and the Fed's decision, with Nasdaq-100 and S&P futures up 0.30% and 0.10% while Dow futures slipped 0.19%. The central bank is expected to keep rates steady in the 3.75% to 4% target range. Oil turned higher: prices climbed Wednesday as investors weighed a prolonged, widening Middle East conflict after Tehran-backed Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia's largest refinery. Brent rose to $115.41 on October 28, up 1.34% from the prior day. Volatility eased into the decision — the VIX closed 17.52, down 4.73%, its lowest since 21 October. This is a live Fed-decision day with an unresolved oil tail — not a clean premium-selling backdrop.
focus.notdown: The boarded bullish names split between a clean breakout and an unverified earnings gap. The cleanest is BUG (Type C, Grade A) — the Global X Cybersecurity ETF logged a breakout above its $50.08 pivot that has held one session on 3.69x volume with a clean structure. APH (Type A, Grade A, bullish) gapped ~6.6% premarket on its Q3 print — analysts expected $0.72 EPS on $9.44B revenue, up 55% and 52% year over year — but the scanner flags the actual EPS/revenue not yet wired and a news 'guidance CUT' that doesn't confirm the bullish gap. Both are watch-only on a RED, Fed-day tape.
focus.notup: Three bearish Type A names boarded — WM, CSGP and NXPI — all gapped down despite mostly solid prints. Waste Management posted adjusted EPS of $2.15, up from $1.98 a year ago but slightly missing the $2.18 consensus, and shares slipped ~3.5%. NXP shares fell nearly 9% after hours despite strong Q3 results, on cautious guidance. CoStar (CSGP) gapped ~7.5% lower despite an EPS beat. But selling bear calls into a VIX-near-17, FOMC-decision tape invites a squeeze on any dovish-Fed or de-escalation headline — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~62 is deep in WARM and P(≥1% gap) at ~43% is well above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. On top of that, the central bank ends its two-day policy meeting today with the rate decision at 2 PM ET and Microsoft and Alphabet report tonight — both inside any normal DTE, an automatic stand-down trigger. The boarded names include one genuinely clean breakout (BUG), but a live Fed decision plus mega-cap prints plus an oil tail is not a tape to underwrite new premium into. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past this afternoon and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.
